entities.summary: Gao Pei was a military general serving under Liu Zhang, ruler of Yi Province, during the Three Kingdoms period of China. He played a crucial role in the Battle of Red Cliffs (208 CE), a pivotal event that shaped the course of the war and ultimately led to the downfall of Cao Cao's regime. Gao Pei's leadership and strategic thinking contributed significantly to the war effort, earning him recognition as one of the most important military leaders of the Three Kingdoms period. His legacy extends beyond his military achievements, as he also played a key role in the development of the Eastern Han dynasty's administrative structures. Despite his importance, Gao Pei's life and achievements are often overlooked in historical accounts, making him a fascinating subject for study and reflection. Through his life and legacy, Gao Pei offers a unique window into the complexities and nuances of ancient Chinese history, revealing the intricate web of alliances, rivalries, and power struggles that defined the Three Kingdoms period.
